denominatorNote: Every fraction in this file is a fraction of the PRE-DILUTION poured volume, never of the finished drink. Published figures disagree with one another on exactly this point — the same drink is described as taking 25% and 50% dilution depending on which volume the percentage is of. Stating the denominator once, here, is what makes the numbers comparable. To read any entry against a final-volume figure, divide by (1 + fraction).

stirred.label: Stirred over ice

source.title: Liquid Intelligence: The Art and Science of the Perfect Cocktail
source.author: Dave Arnold

stirred.note: A closed form in the alcohol by volume of the combined pre-dilution liquid, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1. At the 27% ABV of an equal-parts spirit-and-aperitivo build it returns 0.397, which is 28% of the finished drink — the same figure other sources report as 'about a quarter' when they measure against the glass rather than the pour.

shaken.label: Shaken with ice

source.title: Liquid Intelligence: The Art and Science of the Perfect Cocktail
source.author: Dave Arnold

shaken.note: No closed form comparable to the stirred one has been published for shaking, so this is a stated figure rather than a model. Shaking is far more violent than stirring and takes on correspondingly more water at the same starting strength, and the published band for a standard shake runs from half to three-fifths of the poured volume. The low end of that band is used here.

shaken-long.label: Shaken long — egg, cream or a dry shake first

source.title: Liquid Intelligence: The Art and Science of the Perfect Cocktail
source.author: Dave Arnold

shaken-long.note: A drink shaken to emulsify runs longer than one shaken only to chill, and takes on more water for it. The upper end of the published shaken band.

built-over-ice.label: Built over ice in the glass

source.title: Liquid Intelligence: The Art and Science of the Perfect Cocktail
source.author: Dave Arnold

built-over-ice.note: A built drink is never stirred to equilibrium, so it starts less diluted than a stirred one and keeps diluting in the hand. This figure is the drink as served; a highball finished over twenty minutes ends up well past it.

blended-with-ice.label: Blended with ice

source.title: Liquid Intelligence: The Art and Science of the Perfect Cocktail
source.author: Dave Arnold

blended-with-ice.note: The dilution model does not apply. All of the ice goes into the glass, so it is an authored ingredient line with a mass, not a percentage — and the figure is then measured rather than modelled.

none.label: No ice

source.title: eXir editorial
source.note: Not an external claim: a drink that never meets ice gains no water.

none.note: Hot drinks, brewed drinks and anything poured from a batch at service. Any water in the drink is an authored ingredient line, so the figure is stated rather than modelled and carries no estimate marker.
